title: Map Navigation
description: Navigate midtown Manhattan with the gestures built into the map - drag to pan, the wheel to zoom, right-drag to rotate and tilt - while the center is read back in latitude and longitude.

title: Restrict Map Extent
description: Hold the map inside limits while it runs - RestrictExtent keeps panning inside a box, and MinimumScale and MaximumScale stop it zooming past two scales, each turned on and off live.

title: Vehicle Navigation
description: Follows a vehicle along a GPS route: the camera eases from point to point, turned to the heading and tilted, while the trail grows behind it. Switch to an overview, tilt the camera, or restyle the same tiles dark.

title: Lane-Level Navigation
description: An OpenDRIVE HD map of Wolfsburg - lanes, markings, crossings - handed to the browser whole and drawn by level, while the camera follows a vehicle down the route with lane-level instructions.

title: Zoom to Extents
description: Every way the map can be told where to look - a step, a scale, a layer's bounds, a point, a bearing - with what it looks at read back.

title: Overview Map
description: A small map in the corner shows where the big one is looking and takes it somewhere else with a click.

title: 3D Terrain
description: Raises the Grand Canyon from open elevation tiles and drapes aerial imagery over it, with a relief layer whose style you can edit as the map follows.

title: Perspective & 3D Buildings
description: Tilt and rotate the camera over midtown Manhattan - the buildings are a fill-extrusion layer already in the street style, so they rise and lean with the perspective. The sliders set Pitch and Bearing; a right-drag on the map does the same.

title: The Globe
description: The same vector tiles drawn as a ball. Setting MapView.Projection eases between globe, web mercator and vertical perspective; the tiles never leave web mercator and none is fetched again.

title: Project Features
description: Reprojects features written in decimal degrees into the Spherical Mercator the map is in, and draws them in the browser.

title: Project a Raster
description: Warps a GeoTIFF stored in WGS84 into US National Atlas Equal Area as it is drawn, with a projection converter on the raster's image source.

title: Setting the Projection of a Layer
description: A shapefile in Texas state plane feet drawn on a Web Mercator map: a ProjectionConverter on the source and nothing else changes.

title: Any Projection, Satellite Imagery
description: ThinkGeo Cloud aerial tiles warped into Robinson, Mollweide, Eckert IV and other projections as they are drawn, by a projection converter on the layer, with the classic renderer.

title: Cross the Dateline
description: A Los Angeles to Shanghai great-circle route through the antimeridian, stored with continuous longitudes past -180 and drawn whole - no seam on the globe, one at 180 degrees in Web Mercator, the same data folded back into the world at the tile cut.

title: Vector Map Providers
description: The hosted vector maps, each a style: ThinkGeo Maps light and dark over the same tiles, OpenFreeMap and any other server by its style URL alone.

title: WFS
description: Cadastral parcels from a WFS 2.0 service, fetched by the server as each tile needs them and drawn in the browser.

title: OGC API - Features
description: Named places from an OGC API - Features service, read in latitude and longitude and projected on the server before the tiles are cut.

title: NOAA Weather Stations
description: NOAA's weather stations and their current readings, read live by NoaaWeatherStationFeatureSource and coloured by temperature.

title: NOAA Weather Warnings
description: The warnings NOAA has active right now, read by NoaaWeatherWarningsFeatureSource and coloured by severity.

title: Raster Map Providers
description: The hosted raster maps: ThinkGeo Cloud light, dark, aerial and hybrid, and OpenStreetMap as a raster source in a style document.

title: WMS & WMTS
description: Draw an OGC web service as the map: a WMS layer (mundialis OSM) and a WMTS layer (Swisstopo) requested tile by tile from their servers.

title: Geocoding
description: An address or a place name goes to GeocodingCloudClient and every match comes back as a point with its bounding box; pick one and the map goes there.

title: Reverse Geocoding
description: Click the map and ReverseGeocodingCloudClient answers with the nearest address, the places, roads and addresses within a radius.

title: Routing
description: Stops go to RoutingCloudClient.GetRouteAsync and the route comes back with its turn-by-turn segments; click the map to add a stop.

title: Routing: Service Area
description: How far 15, 30, 45 and 60 minutes of driving reach from a point, one polygon per limit from RoutingCloudClient.GetServiceAreaAsync.

title: Routing: Traveling Salesperson
description: Stops in no particular order go to RoutingCloudClient.GetOptimizedRouteAsync, which answers with the order of the shortest round trip.

title: Elevation
description: A point, a line or an area drawn on the map is sampled by ElevationCloudClient; a line's samples draw as a profile.

title: Time Zone
description: Click anywhere and TimeZoneCloudClient answers with the zone, the local time there and the zone's outline.

title: Projection
description: Well known text in latitude and longitude goes to ProjectionCloudClient and comes back in the map's meters.

title: Color Utilities
description: ColorCloudClient hands back a family of colours that go together; six of them class Frisco's census block groups by housing units.

title: World Maps Query
description: The features behind ThinkGeo's world map asked for by a shape you draw: containing, intersecting, overlapping, within or nearest, with MapsQueryCloudClient.

title: Vector File Formats
description: Open a vector file - a shapefile, GeoJSON, KML, GPX, MapInfo TAB, TinyGeo, an S-57 chart - or build features in code; reading the format is the only line that differs. The overlay cuts it into tiles and one editable style draws them all.

title: Raster File Formats
description: Open a raster file - a NAIP GeoTIFF, a plain JPEG with its world file, ECW, or anything else GDAL reads - through the raster layer named after the format, warped into the map's projection as it is drawn.

title: Databases
description: Open a table from a database - SQLite, a GeoPackage, an Esri file geodatabase, PostgreSQL / PostGIS or SQL Server; the connection is the only line that differs.

title: Shape Operations
description: Buffer, union, intersect, difference, simplify, convex hull and more, run on shapes drawn on the map and animated as the parameter changes.

title: Shape Measurements
description: Area, length, perimeter, distance and the point nearest to a click, measured on Frisco parks and trails in the unit you choose.

title: Find Features by Spatial Relation
description: Draw a shape and find the zoning parcels that contain, intersect, touch, cross or lie within a distance of it, with QueryTools.

title: Get Data from One Feature
description: Click a park and read every column its record holds, found with a point-in-polygon query and shown in a popup.

title: Check If Features Are Equal
description: Click a zoning parcel and find every other parcel with topologically equal geometry, whatever the order of its vertices.

title: Validate Topology
description: Twenty-five topology rules - no overlaps, no gaps, endpoints covered, and more - each checked with TopologyValidator and drawn with the shapes that break it.

title: Style Layer Toggles
description: Every layer of the basemap's style, listed with a checkbox. SetLayerVisibility switches any of them at runtime - the document records it, the map skips that layer as it draws, and no tile is fetched again.

title: Insert a Layer Under the Labels
description: A translucent wash placed above the streets and below the labels with InsertLayerAt(StyleLayerSlot.UnderLabels) - a spot in the layer stack an overlay, always on top of everything, can never reach.

title: Render Points, Lines and Polygons
description: Style points, lines and polygons from three shapefiles, and label each of them, from the style document beside the map - edit it and the map follows.

title: Render Based on Rules
description: One dataset, four expressions - match, step, filter and case: value, class-break, filter and boolean-expression styling are one mechanism, an expression in the layer's paint.

title: US Demographic Map
description: A choropleth of the 2010 US census - each state coloured by the class its value falls in, with the breaks taken from the data. A step expression on the chosen column, drawn in the browser, with a legend read from the same breaks.

title: Advanced Labels
description: Six label lessons on crafted data - text bends along its line, anchors from its own column, yields to priority, wraps and recases, keeps its icon when the name cannot fit, and writes CJK vertically. Each is a style.json beside the map, editable while it runs.

title: Heatmap
description: A heatmap layer over point sightings: the document decides what each sighting weighs, and radius, intensity, opacity and the color ramp are live controls changed in place.

title: Display Cluster Points
description: Hundreds of points handed to the browser and grouped there - VectorTileOverlay.Cluster turns the source into a clustered one, and the style draws each cluster as a numbered circle that splits as the map zooms in.

title: Your Features, Two Ways
description: The same application data - drawn shapes, placed markers, labels - once the classic way with a LayerOverlay rendered on the server, and once the new way with a MapStyle drawn in the browser. Hide a shape on each and watch what it costs.

title: Create a Multi-Column Text Style
description: Label world capitals with their name and population from two columns, using a concat expression in text-field.

title: Display Dot Density
description: Owner- and renter-occupied housing as dots scattered inside each state, one per 25,000 units, generated once as data and coloured by the style.

title: Hatch Styles
description: Every GeoHatchStyle drawn once by AreaStyle.CreateHatchStyle, added to the style's images, and tiled across the parks by fill-pattern.

title: Migrate a Classic Layer
description: Five classic FeatureLayers with their ZoomLevelSet styles, drawn on the server on one map and put through FeatureLayerTranslator on the other, with the style.json it wrote and what it could not carry.

title: Isolines
description: Isolines over scattered readings: the field is interpolated on the server - inverse distance weighting over a grid - and traced into features there; the browser draws them, coloured, banded and labelled by level.

title: Wind as a Vector Field
description: NDFD surface wind read from two GeoTIFF bands with GDAL and drawn as a field of arrows, each turned where the wind goes and sized and coloured by speed.

title: NEXRAD Weather Radar
description: Live US weather radar drawn over the basemap as a raster tile source the browser reads directly, animating the last hour of the national reflectivity mosaic from the Iowa Environmental Mesonet.

title: Dynamic Rendering
description: State populations since 1900 as circles that grow and change colour as a year slider moves; the features travel once and only the style expressions change.

title: Legend
description: A classic LegendAdornmentLayer, one item per class of the style, drawn on the server by the AdornmentOverlay and laid over the map.

title: Scale Line and Scale Bar
description: The classic scale line and scale bar adornments, drawn again each time the map stops moving.

title: Magnetic North
description: True north, magnetic north and the declination between them for the middle of the map, from the MagneticDeclinationAdornmentLayer.

title: Map Tool Controls
description: The zoom bar map tool, scale line and logo adornments, and the pointer's coordinates from OnMouseMove in the form you pick.

title: Markers
description: Images the browser keeps pinned to places, from a SimpleMarkerOverlay: click the map to drop one, click a marker for its details.

title: Popups
description: A popup per hotel from a shapefile, each a piece of the page the browser keeps anchored to its place.

title: Animated Marker
description: A marker whose SVG image animates itself in the browser; a button swaps it for a still one.

title: Custom Feature Sources
description: A FeatureSource of your own: one class, one overridden method that reads a CSV of coordinates, and the map treats it like any shapefile.

title: Mark the Places
description: Shows how to mark a place with beautiful icons and detailed information.

title: Popup
description: Shows how to display a popup balloon with images and descriptions included.

title: Draw and Modify Geometries
description: Shows how to draw and modify the geometries loaded on the map.

title: Measure Distance & Area
description: Demonstrates how to measure distances and areas on the map.

title: Export the Map as an Image
description: Save the current map view as a PNG - the map's own WebGL canvas, read back at screen resolution and handed to the browser to download.
